admission.justification: The rule is guarded end to end by the new module's grouped-deletion, reworded-group, single-source, overview and author-supplied-sources cases, whose grouped proof runs the leaf's own worklist into the writer and back. Leaving it unstated costs a whole group: L56's two deleted c-05 skill files carry nine identical copies each, so their card items could not be answered at all and its memory check kept four findings.

applicability: Every onboarding-trace row the file writer authors for a card subject -- a file-level card or a route overview -- in a converted memory worktree.
conditions: The leaf's persisted worklist holds an onboarding_trace item naming the subject, so the row binds that item's sources with their candidate blobs, `absent` for a deleted source.
A card subject no worklist item names is a file card and binds its own path.
An item that names only the card's own path yields the same one-source row as before.
A route overview no worklist item covers is refused with the original no-worklist-item problem instead of falling back to a path.
exclusions: The onboarding-trace gate, the worklist's grouping and the item contract are unchanged, and RowRequest still holds no sources field: a hand-off that supplies one is refused.
No other row kind -- invariant, family, dependency, unexplained-change, planned, reconsideration, membership or record -- takes its sources this way.
A card's row proves that the item is answered, not that the whole Python suite, an installed host or a fresh Curator execution passed.
statement: When the item of a file card covers a group of identical copies of its source, the knowledge writer's row for that card binds every source of the item, so that the row can answer the item.
